scenes.line1: Why do apps fail right after go-live?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why so many apps break right after launch? Let's nail the classic onboarding failures every engineer should know cold.

scenes.label: Probe
scenes.sub: Health checks need authentication, or redirect to SSO, so every backend looks unhealthy.
scenes.say: First, health probes that require authentication or redirect to single sign-on make all your backends look unhealthy. Easy to miss, but brutal in production.

rows.b: NSG denies above load balancer rule
No intermediate or subject alt name

scenes.say: Next up: firewall rules that block load balancer probes, DNS that returns the wrong address for private endpoints, and certificates missing intermediate or subject alt names. Each one can kill your onboarding.

scenes.question: Why can't the load balancer reach the app?
scenes.wrong: The app is bound to all interfaces.
scenes.right: The app is bound only to the loopback address, so the load balancer can't connect.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: if the load balancer can't reach your app, check if it's bound only to the loopback address. That's a rookie mistake.
